By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by section 2 of the Civil Service Act  
(22 Stat. 403) and section 1753 of the  
Revised Statutes of the United States  
(5 U.S.C. 631), and as President of the  
United States, it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
S e c t io n 1. Whenever a Federal em­
ployee or former Federal employee has  
met the requirements of an Executive  
order (heretofore or hereafter issued)  
which provides a benefit for Federal em­
ployees but has become ineligible to re­
ceive such benefit solely because of the  
failure of an administrative agency, be­
cause of'error or oversight, to make a  
timely determination or recommenda­
tion required by the Executive order,  
the Civil Service Commission may, to  
avoid inequity in individual cases, con­
fer such benefit upon the employee or  
former employee: Provided, that the

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 authorizes the Civil Service Commission to confer a benefit provided by an Executive order on an employee or former employee who became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes it and not retroactively; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions effective before the agency was notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954, a one-time command complete in 1959. Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 amended the clause by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Office for the Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404; before and after the change the authority is the same, and the amendment renames the actor. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, 5 CFR 351.502 still refers to cases under it, and its cited statutory authority survives in 5 U.S.C. 3301, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (24 FR 5233, signed 1959-06-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10826.txt): section 1 lets the Civil Service Commission confer a benefit under an Executive order on a Federal employee or former employee who met its requirements but became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes the required determination, with no action effective before the date it is taken; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions made effective before the agency is notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note 'Amended by: EO 12107, December 28, 1978'; the held text of Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28) section 2-101 amends and revises each listed order, among them 10826, by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, and section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979, so the amendment is recorded as a later event and does not end the order. current-law:usc has 0 hits (no U.S. Code note names the order). current-law:ecfr has 3 hits: 5 CFR 351.501 and 5 CFR 351.502, whose eCFR text (351.502 in effect on 2026-09-02) still refers to cases under Executive Order 10826 to correct certain administrative errors, pending resolution by OPM. The authority the order cites, section 2 of the Civil Service Act and Revised Statutes 1753 (5 U.S.C. 631), is the derivation of 5 U.S.C. 3301 (Pub. L. 89-554, 1966), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which still authorizes the President to prescribe regulations for admission into the civil service and was amended by Pub. L. 119-60 on December 18, 2025. The held-corpus search for the order's number found no revocation or supersession.

Executive Order 12107's substitution of the Office of Personnel Management is an amendment of the same clause, not a separate command."}
